outcome: No result since 26 January 2024 decides whether a class of models of a countable theory omitting countably many types, with a model of size ℵ_ω1, must have a model of size continuum; the only post-freeze event bearing on it (Marangelis, arXiv 2410.19515, Oct 2024) addresses a higher-cardinal analogue and states that the ℵ_ω1 conjecture it discusses is not refuted, and Shelah's open question about the negation of his conjecture remains open.
problem_asks: (1) K is the class of models of a countable first-order theory T that omits countably many types (the bullet does not say the omitted types are non-isolated, nor fix the language beyond countability). (2) Hypothesis: K has a model of cardinality ℵ_ω1. (3) Question: does K then have a model of cardinality continuum (2^ℵ0)? The bullet states no cardinal-arithmetic hypothesis, so as written it is a universal yes/no claim over all such T and all such omitted families. Shelah's own form of the question for L_ω1,ω-sentences (Sh:702 Question 1.13; Baldwin–Boney 2015 Question 4.0.2 item 5) carries the extra hypothesis ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0; the bullet does not.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'Borel sets with large squares' (Sh:522), arXiv math/9802134 v1, posted 15 Feb 1998; Fund. Math. 159 (1999) 1–50. Its abstract states the L_ω1,ω condition ⊗′_μ: if ψ ∈ L_ω1,ω has a model of cardinality μ then it has a model of cardinality continuum. It shows ⊗′_μ is equivalent to Borel conditions ⊗_μ and ⊕_μ under MA + 2^ℵ0 > μ. Per the ar5iv introduction, after adding more than ℵ_ω1 Cohen reals to a GCH universe the L_ω1,ω Hanf number below the continuum is ℵ_ω1 (attributed there to Hodges, and to Hrushovski and Velickovic); the paper leaves open whether λ_ω1(ℵ0) = ℵ_ω1 in ZFC. Later papers (Sinapova–Souldatos 2017, Marangelis 2024) report that Shelah proves in this paper the consistency of the conjecture that if ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0 and an L_ω1,ω-sentence has a model of size ℵ_ω1 then it has a model of size 2^ℵ0.
events.revisions: arXiv v2 (listed 28 Sep 2022 in a search snippet, not checked against the listing) and v3 revised 1 May 2023 per the arXiv abstract page; journal Fund. Math. 159 (1999).
events.delivers: Consistency only, not a ZFC answer. In the consistency model described in the introduction (ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0 after Cohen reals over GCH) the ℵ_ω1 → continuum transfer holds for L_ω1,ω-sentences. Under MA + 2^ℵ0 > μ the Borel and L_ω1,ω forms coincide. The result is stated for L_ω1,ω-sentences, not for classes of models of a countable theory omitting countably many types, and it depends on the hypothesis ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0 or on MA.
events.remains: The bullet's ZFC question for omitting-types classes with no cardinal-arithmetic hypothesis; whether λ_ω1(ℵ0) = ℵ_ω1 in ZFC (open per the paper); whether the negation of the conjecture is consistent (open per Marangelis 2024).

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, Fund. Math. 159 (1999) 1–50

events.time_since_posted: Not applicable; later papers cite it (Baldwin–Boney 2015 cites [She99b], which the ar5iv text identifies as this paper; Sinapova–Souldatos 2017 and Marangelis 2024 cite it).
events.direction: Cuts toward the expected positive answer (a continuum-sized model is forced), but only as a consistency result under cardinal-arithmetic hypotheses (ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0, or MA + 2^ℵ0 > μ).

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'On what I do not understand (and have something to say), model theory' (Sh:702), arXiv math/9910158. In §1 ('Two cardinal theorems'), Question 1.13 asks, for ψ in L_ω1,ω with a model of cardinality at least ℵ_ω1, whether ψ has a model of cardinality continuum, 'well assuming 2^ℵ0 > ℵ_ω1'. Question 1.15 asks the Borel-rectangle analogue. The paper poses these questions and reports no answer to them.
events.revisions: Not checked beyond the arXiv identifier.
events.delivers: Nothing: it poses the question for L_ω1,ω-sentences under the hypothesis 2^ℵ0 > ℵ_ω1. It is the earliest source I found that states the ℵ_ω1 / continuum question in this form; I did not establish that it is the source of the bullet, which is in omitting-types form and carries no hypothesis.
events.time_since_posted: About 27 years; restated as open in Baldwin–Boney (2015) and Sinapova–Souldatos (2017).

events.what_happened: Baldwin, Boney and co-authors, 'Hanf Numbers and Presentation Theorems in AECs', arXiv 1511.02935 (Nov 2015). Section 4, Question 4.0.2, item 5 lists as open, attributed to Shelah: 'If ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0, does an L_ω1,ω-sentence with models up to ℵ_ω1 have a model in 2^ℵ0?', noting that Shelah proves this statement consistent in [She99b], which the paper's bibliography identifies as Sh:522.
events.delivers: Nothing: restates Shelah's L_ω1,ω question under the hypothesis ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0 as open.
events.time_since_posted: About 11 years as of 2026; the item is still listed as open in the paper.

events.what_happened: Sinapova and Souldatos, 'Kurepa trees and spectra of L_ω1,ω-sentences', arXiv 1705.05821 (May 2017). It builds a single L_ω1,ω-sentence ψ coding Kurepa trees. Corollary 2.14: it is consistent that 2^ℵ0 < ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ1 and some L_ω1,ω-sentence has models of size ℵ_ω1 and none of size 2^ℵ1, so 2^ℵ0 cannot be replaced by 2^ℵ1 in Shelah's conjecture. The introduction says ψ always has a model of size 2^ℵ0, so ψ does not refute the conjecture. Section 4, Question 4.0.2 item 5 restates Shelah's question.
events.revisions: v1 and v2 exist (a search snippet notes that reference numbering differs between them); I read only the ar5iv rendering.
events.delivers: A consistency result about a different sentence and a different replacement of 2^ℵ0 (by 2^ℵ1), in a model where 2^ℵ0 < ℵ_ω1, so the conjecture's hypothesis fails there. It does not produce a model of size continuum for any class with a model of size ℵ_ω1 under the bullet's hypotheses. Restriction: it is a consistency result and the sentence is a specific L_ω1,ω-sentence.
events.time_since_posted: About 9 years; the question it restates is still listed as open in the paper.
events.direction: Does not bear on the bullet's direction: it shows only that the conjecture's continuum-sized conclusion cannot be obtained by replacing 2^ℵ0 with 2^ℵ1 in general.
events.object: The L_ω1,ω-sentence ψ coding Kurepa trees (a sentence defined by a syntactic construction; its spectrum in the constructed models is established by forcing, so the model-existence claims are non-constructive consistency results).

events.what_happened: Baldwin and Laskowski, 'Henkin constructions of models with size continuum', arXiv 1710.00422 (1 Oct 2017); Bull. Symb. Logic 25 (2019) 1–33. A survey of constructing models of size continuum in ω steps. The abstract also records a new joint theorem with Shelah that a pseudominimal theory has an atomic model of size continuum. The body (read via search snippets, not opened) records the Chang and Lopez-Escobar correspondence: for any L_ω1,ω-sentence there is a countable expansion, a first-order theory T and a partial type Δ such that the sentence's models are the reducts of models of T omitting Δ. It also records Shelah's result that if an L_ω1,ω-sentence has a model of size λ_ω1(ℵ0) then it has a model of size 2^ℵ0.
events.revisions: Single version per the arXiv abstract page; journal Bull. Symb. Logic 25 (2019).
events.delivers: Nothing on the bullet. It is the background bridge: Chang and Lopez-Escobar take an L_ω1,ω-sentence to an omitting-types class in one direction, which is why the bullet and Shelah's L_ω1,ω question are close neighbours. It does not establish the converse, nor that the two questions coincide.

events.direction: No direction on the bullet: background and a survey.

events.what_happened: Baldwin, Laskowski and Shelah, 'When does ℵ1-categoricity imply ω-stability?', arXiv 2308.13942 (26 Aug 2023); Model Theory 3 (2024) 801–823, DOI 10.2140/mt.2024.3.801. The abstract: if an atomic class is ℵ1-categorical and has a model of size (2^ℵ0)^+, then it is ω-stable. The paper's background discusses the Hanf number and continuum, and the role of Chang's translation of L_ω1,ω-sentences into omitting-types classes.
events.revisions: v1 only per the arXiv abstract page; journal version 2024.
events.delivers: Concerns ℵ1-categorical atomic classes and the size (2^ℵ0)^+. It does not establish or refute that a class with a model of size ℵ_ω1 has a model of size continuum. Discounted as a different question.
events.direction: Does not bear on the bullet's direction; a neighbouring result on atomic classes.

events.what_happened: Marangelis, 'Shelah's conjecture fails for higher cardinalities', arXiv 2410.19515 (25 Oct 2024), single author, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (PhD work under Ioannis Souldatos). It constructs an L_ω1,ω-sentence ψ_α coding ℵ_α+1-Kurepa trees (α countable). It shows it is consistent that 2^ℵα < 2^ℵα+1, that 2^ℵα+1 is weakly inaccessible, and that the spectrum of ψ_α is [ℵ0, 2^ℵα+1). Its consequence: if 2^ℵ0 is replaced by 2^ℵα+1, it is consistent that there is no local Hanf number. The paper says ψ_α always has a model of size 2^ℵ0, so it does not refute Shelah's original conjecture. It lists as open Question 1.3: is the negation of Shelah's conjecture consistent with ZFC? It also states that Shelah and D. Ulrich generalised the conjecture to higher cardinals and proved consistency results for local Hanf numbers above the continuum, which are unpublished (reported second-hand; no document found).
events.revisions: v1 only, per arXiv abstract page and searches; no journal version found.
events.delivers: A consistency result for a higher-cardinal analogue: local Hanf numbers can consistently fail when 2^ℵ0 is replaced by 2^ℵα+1. Restrictions: the analogue (ℵ_α+1 and α countable, not ℵ_ω1 below the continuum); consistency only; the paper states the conjecture for ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0 is not refuted by its sentence.
events.remains: The bullet as stated: whether a model of size ℵ_ω1 forces a model of size continuum for omitting-types classes in ZFC, with or without the hypothesis ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0. Also open per the paper: whether the negation of Shelah's conjecture is consistent.
events.time_since_posted: About 23 months as of 11 Oct 2026. No citing paper, journal version, review or verification found. Google Scholar, Semantic Scholar and NASA ADS citation pages were not reachable.
events.direction: Cuts against uniform transfer for the higher analogue (the constructed sentence has no model at 2^ℵα+1 in the consistency model), but the paper explicitly says it does not refute the ℵ_ω1 case, which remains open.
events.object: The L_ω1,ω-sentence ψ_α, which codes ℵ_α+1-Kurepa trees. In a consistency model it has a model of every cardinality in [ℵ0, 2^ℵα+1) and none at 2^ℵα+1. The claim is established by forcing, so it is a non-constructive consistency result, not an explicit model.

events.what_happened: Baldwin, Laskowski and Shelah, 'An analogue of U-rank for atomic classes', arXiv 2502.00984 (3 Feb 2025). For a countable complete first-order T it studies the class of atomic models; if some tp(d/a) is not ranked, there are 2^ℵ1 non-isomorphic models of size ℵ1 in the class.
events.revisions: v1 only per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Counting non-isomorphic atomic models at ℵ1. It does not mention Hanf numbers, omitting types, ℵ_ω1 or continuum. Discounted as a different question.

events.what_happened: John T. Baldwin, talk at the conference in honour of Shelah's 80th birthday, TU Wien, July 2025. The schedule gives the title 'When is an ℵ1-categorical L_ω1,ω-sentence ω-stable?' (Monday 14 July). The archived slides carry the title 'Can categorical classes in L_ω1,ω be bounded in size?' and the date 16 July 2025, with sections including 'Getting Models in the continuum'. I could not read the slides (the PDF returned binary), so the talk's content on the continuum is unverified.
events.revisions: Slides and schedule disagree on the date (14 vs 16 July) and on the title; not resolved.
events.delivers: Nothing I could verify. A talk outline on the same questions; it reports no new theorem that I could read.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as far as I could establish.
events.doubts: The slides were unreadable to me, so I cannot say whether they state a result on the bullet's question.
events.direction: Unknown for the bullet; the talk's title suggests the question of bounded size of categorical L_ω1,ω-classes, not the continuum transfer.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'The Hanf number of omitting complete types', Pacific J. Math. 50 (1974) 163–168. It shows the Hanf number for omitting complete types by models of complete countable theories equals that for omitting possibly incomplete types by models of countable theories. Its Hanf numbers are on the beth scale (ℶ_α); the paper does not treat ℵ_ω1 versus continuum.
events.revisions: Not checked; the date is the journal year, and the first public version may be earlier.
events.delivers: Nothing on the bullet's question; it is about the size threshold for omission (beth scale). Discounted as a neighbouring omitting-types result.

summary: I ran 42 web searches and opened about 13 sources; the frozen bullet text was checked in the repo's page.wiki (line 402), which has no citation on it. No paper found since 26 January 2024 decides the bullet's question, in ZFC or consistently, for classes of models of a countable theory omitting countably many types. The bullet's question is the omitting-types form of a question Shelah posed for L_ω1,ω-sentences: Sh:702 Question 1.13 (1999) asks whether such a sentence with a model of size at least ℵ_ω1 has a model of continuum size, assuming 2^ℵ0 > ℵ_ω1, and Baldwin–Boney (2015) Question 4.0.2 item 5 restates it with that hypothesis. I could not confirm that the bullet's source is either of these. Shelah's Sh:522 (1998/1999) proves the consistency of the L_ω1,ω version, and Sinapova–Souldatos (2017) show consistency results for a related sentence, but neither answers the bullet in ZFC. The Chang–Lopez-Escobar correspondence, as recorded in Baldwin–Laskowski (2017; body read through a search snippet, not opened), takes each L_ω1,ω-sentence to an omitting-types class in one direction; I did not establish the converse, so I cannot say that the bullet's class and Shelah's L_ω1,ω question are the same question. The only post-freeze event bearing on the question is Marangelis (arXiv 2410.19515, 25 Oct 2024), a single-author v1 preprint with no journal version, citing work, or review found. It shows that replacing 2^ℵ0 by 2^ℵα+1 can consistently yield no local Hanf number, says its sentence always has a model of size 2^ℵ0 and so does not refute Shelah's conjecture at ℵ_ω1, and lists the negation's consistency as open. Two other post-freeze items (Baldwin–Laskowski–Shelah 2025 on atomic-class U-rank; Baldwin's July 2025 talk, whose slides I could not read) do not appear to touch the question. The live Wikipedia bullet now cites [162] and the frozen revision does not; I could not reach the text of [162]. The Shelah–Ulrich unpublished generalisation mentioned by Marangelis has no public document I could find. AI involvement: none found in any source I read. I searched explicitly for AI involvement (Shelah with AI terms; local Hanf number with GPT, Claude and Gemini; Erdős-problem trackers; Epoch's FrontierMath: Open Problems; OpenAI's 722-manuscript release; Google DeepMind's 2026 work; Terence Tao's 2026 commentary). The Epoch tracker page I opened shows 10 of about 50 problems, none in logic or set theory; the rest sit behind 'See more', which I did not open. The OpenAI repository front page I opened lists nine reasoning-summary families, none in logic; a third-party index I saw in a search snippet lists six 'mathematical logic' families among OpenAI's 372, which I could not verify because I did not open the full catalogue. That catalogue is the main gap in the AI search.
competing_reading: (a) Read the bullet literally, without Shelah's hypothesis ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0, which the bullet omits. Then cases with 2^ℵ0 ≥ ℵ_ω1 are also in scope, and I did not research them. For example, under GCH (2^ℵ0 = ℵ1 < ℵ_ω1) the bullet asks whether a model of size ℵ_ω1 forces one of size ℵ1. My own reasoning, unverified against a source: for L_ω1,ω-definable classes downward Löwenheim–Skolem would seem to give a model of size ℵ1, but I did not establish whether that transfers to omitting-types classes. (b) Read Marangelis's title ('Shelah's conjecture fails for higher cardinalities') as a negative resolution of the bullet. Its text says the opposite: the constructed sentence has a model of size 2^ℵ0 and the ℵ_ω1 conjecture is not refuted. (c) Read Sh:522's consistency result as a partial positive answer to the bullet. It is a consistency result under hypotheses the bullet does not state, so it does not answer the bullet as written.
what_would_settle_it: The text of reference [162] on the live Wikipedia page, which would show what source the bullet rests on and whether it carries the hypothesis ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0. The full text of Sh:522 and Sh:702 for an omitting-types formulation with no cardinal-arithmetic hypothesis. A ZFC result on whether λ_ω1(ℵ0) = ℵ_ω1, or on the consistency of the negation of Shelah's conjecture. The journal version of Marangelis's paper, or any citing paper that treats the ℵ_ω1 case. The full openai/math catalogue (for any logic family) and the hidden problems on Epoch's tracker.

incomplete: (1) The reference text for [162] on the live Wikipedia page was not reached (the page's reference list was truncated in every fetch), and the frozen revision carries no citation, so I cannot say which source the bullet rests on. (2) The Sh:522, Sh:702, Baldwin–Boney and Sinapova–Souldatos details come from WebFetch summaries of their ar5iv renderings, not from a reading of the full text; the question numbers and quotes are as those summaries report them. (3) The bodies of Baldwin–Laskowski 2017 (1710.00422), Baldwin–Laskowski–Shelah 2023 (2308.13942) and 2025 (2502.00984) were not read; only abstracts were opened, and statements about their bodies come from search snippets. (4) The Baldwin 2025 slides were unreadable and the talk's date and title conflict across sources; I could not verify what the talk says about the continuum. (5) Citation checks for Marangelis 2024 were not possible beyond search results. (6) The OpenAI 722-manuscript catalogue (including any 'mathematical logic' families) and the hidden problems on Epoch's tracker were not checked; this is the main gap in the AI search. (7) Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures repository and the Erdős problems wiki were not opened. (8) The Shelah–Ulrich claim has no public source. (9) The Chang–Lopez-Escobar converse, and whether the bullet's omitting-types class is equivalent to Shelah's L_ω1,ω question, were not established.

judgement.why: The statement asks a ZFC yes/no question for omitting-types classes. Sh:522 proves only that a positive answer (for L_ω1,ω sentences, under ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0) is consistent. A consistency result under extra hypotheses answers a changed question, so it is variant rather than case. Marangelis 2024, the only post-snapshot event with mathematical content, treats a higher-cardinal analogue and says explicitly that it does not touch the ℵ_ω1 case: variant. Sinapova–Souldatos (replacing 2^ℵ0 by 2^ℵ1), BLS 2023/2025 and Shelah 1974 address neighbouring questions: variant. The question-posing papers, the survey and the unread talk settle nothing: none. No AI involvement was found anywhere in the record.
judgement.doubts: The Baldwin 2025 talk slides could not be read, so a result in them cannot be excluded. The AI search left the OpenAI catalogue and Epoch's hidden problems unchecked. Read literally, the statement has no ℵ_ω1 < 2^ℵ0 hypothesis, and the record did not explore the case 2^ℵ0 ≤ ℵ_ω1. That case may be trivial or classical, but it is not evidenced here.
